title: Chicken katsu curry
summary: Crispy panko chicken served over rice with a mild, richly spiced Japanese curry sauce.
method: Cook the onion and carrot in a saucepan with a little oil over medium heat until softened. Add the potato and water, then simmer until tender.
Turn off the heat and dissolve the curry roux a little at a time. Return to a gentle simmer until glossy and thick.
Flatten the chicken breasts to 1.5 cm, season, then coat in flour, egg and panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Shallow-fry the chicken in hot oil over medium heat until golden on both sides and 75°C in the centre.
Rest briefly, slice and serve with the rice and curry.

stages.title: Start curry base
steps: Cook onion and carrot in a saucepan with a little oil over medium heat until softened.
Add potato and water; simmer until the vegetables are tender.

stages.title: Finish curry
steps: Turn off the heat and dissolve curry roux blocks a little at a time.
Return to a gentle simmer, stirring until glossy and thick.

stages.title: Crumb chicken
steps: Flatten breasts to even 1.5 cm thickness and season.
Coat in flour, beaten egg and panko, pressing crumbs firmly into the meat.

stages.title: Cook cutlets
steps: Shallow-fry in hot oil over medium heat until golden on both sides.
Check the centre reaches 75°C, rest briefly and slice; serve with rice and curry.

tips: Keep the curry at a gentle simmer after adding roux so it does not catch.
variations: Replace chicken with breaded aubergine and use vegetable curry roux.
storage: Refrigerate curry and chicken separately up to 3 days; re-crisp chicken in oven.

title: Seafood paella
summary: Saffron rice studded with seafood, peppers and peas, cooked until a crisp socarrat forms underneath.
method: Heat the olive oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat and soften the capsicum for about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, grated tomatoes and smoked paprika. Cook for about 7 minutes, until reduced to a thick paste.
Stir in the bomba rice to coat it, then add the hot fish stock with the saffron and spread the rice evenly.
Simmer without stirring for 8–10 minutes, adjusting the heat to keep a gentle bubble. Arrange the prawns and mussels on top.
Cook for another 8–10 minutes, until the prawns are opaque and the mussels have opened. Discard any that stay closed, rest covered for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.

stages.title: Prepare sofrito
steps: Heat oil in a wide paella pan over medium heat and soften capsicum for about 5 minutes, until soft.
Add garlic, grated tomato and paprika; cook until reduced to a thick paste.

stages.title: Toast rice
steps: Stir in rice so each grain is coated in the sofrito.
Add saffron-infused hot stock and distribute rice evenly across the pan.

stages.title: Cook undisturbed
steps: Simmer without stirring for 8–10 minutes, adjusting heat to maintain a gentle bubbling surface.
Arrange prawns and mussels on top and cook for the final 8–10 minutes, until prawns are opaque and mussels have opened.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Check prawns are opaque and mussels have opened; discard any that remain closed.
Rest paella covered loosely for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.

tips: Avoid stirring after adding stock so the rice can form a crisp base.
variations: Use squid rings or firm white fish in place of some prawns.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 2 days; reheat seafood thoroughly once.

title: Kimchi fried rice
summary: Day-old rice stir-fried with tangy kimchi, sesame oil and a golden fried egg.
method: Break up the chilled rice and chop the kimchi. Mix the gochujang, kimchi juice and soy sauce into a sauce.
Heat the neutral oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the kimchi for about 4 minutes, until the edges caramelise and the pan looks less wet.
Add the rice and sauce, tossing to coat. Press the rice against the pan for a few minutes, until crisp in spots.
Stir through the sesame oil and sliced spring onions until heated through.
Fry the eggs separately until the whites are fully set and the yolks are done how you like them. Top the rice with the eggs and sesame seeds.

stages.title: Prepare ingredients
steps: Break up chilled rice with clean hands or a fork so there are no large clumps.
Chop kimchi and mix gochujang with kimchi juice and soy sauce.

stages.title: Fry kimchi
steps: Heat neutral oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook kimchi until its edges start to caramelise and the pan looks less wet.

stages.title: Fry rice
steps: Add rice and toss with kimchi sauce, pressing it against the pan briefly to crisp.
Stir through sesame oil and sliced spring onions.

stages.title: Finish with eggs
steps: Fry eggs separately until whites are fully set and yolks reach your preferred doneness.
Top rice with eggs and sesame seeds.

tips: Use rice chilled promptly after cooking and stored in the fridge; do not leave cooked rice out overnight.
variations: Add diced spam or cooked tofu for extra protein.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 1 day and reheat thoroughly only once.

title: Palak paneer
summary: Soft paneer cubes in a velvety spinach curry scented with garlic, ginger and garam masala.
method: Wilt the spinach in boiling water, then cool in cold water. Drain well and blend with a splash of water until smooth.
Heat the ghee in a pan over medium heat. Sizzle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds, then cook the onion until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic, chilli, tomatoes and turmeric. Cook until thick.
Stir in the spinach purée and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Add the garam masala and cream, loosening with a little water if needed.
Add the paneer and heat gently for 3–4 minutes until warmed through. Season, and serve with roti or rice if using.

stages.title: Blanch spinach
steps: Wilt spinach briefly in boiling water, then transfer to cold water.
Drain thoroughly and blend with a splash of water until smooth.

stages.title: Make masala
steps: Heat ghee and sizzle cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Cook onion over medium heat until golden, then add ginger, garlic, chilli, tomatoes and turmeric until thick.

stages.title: Combine sauce
steps: Stir spinach purée into masala and simmer gently for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add garam masala and cream, loosening with water if needed.

stages.title: Warm paneer
steps: Add paneer cubes and heat gently until warmed through.
Season and serve with roti or rice; avoid boiling hard or paneer may toughen.

tips: Avoid overcooking spinach to preserve its bright green colour.
variations: Use firm tofu and coconut cream for a dairy-free version.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently.

title: Piri piri chicken
summary: Juicy chicken marinated in fiery piri piri, lemon and garlic, roasted until charred at the edges.
method: Blend the chillies, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, oregano, oil and salt into a marinade. Taste and adjust the heat.
Pat the chicken dry and score the thick parts. Coat in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes if time allows.
Arrange the chicken skin-side up on a rack over a tray. Roast at 200°C for about 35 minutes, turning the tray halfway, until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Rest the chicken for 5–10 minutes so the juices settle.
Serve with lemon wedges and roasted potatoes, if using.

stages.title: Blend marinade
steps: Blend chillies, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, oregano, oil and salt.
Taste the marinade before it touches raw chicken and adjust heat.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Pat chicken dry and score thick sections lightly.
Coat evenly with marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes if time allows.

stages.title: Roast chicken
steps: Arrange pieces skin-side up on a rack over a tray and roast at 200°C.
Turn tray halfway and cook until thickest part of each piece reaches 75°C.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest chicken 5–10 minutes so juices settle.
Serve with lemon wedges and roasted potatoes.

tips: Keep a separate portion of marinade for serving; never reuse raw-chicken marinade without boiling it.
variations: Use boneless thighs and shorten cooking time, checking temperature.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze cooked chicken up to 2 months.

title: Thai basil chicken (pad krapow)
summary: Minced chicken flash-fried with garlic, chilli and holy basil, served over rice.
ingredients: 1 handful Thai holy basil or Thai basil
method: Rinse the jasmine rice and cook on low heat per the packet until tender. Keep covered and warm.
Stir the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar together. Finely chop the garlic and chillies.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the garlic and chilli briefly until fragrant.
Add the chicken mince, breaking it up, and cook until cooked through (75°C), about 6 minutes.
Add the sauce and toss until it coats the meat and reduces slightly.
Turn off the heat, fold in the basil and serve over the rice.

stages.title: Cook rice
steps: Rinse rice and cook according to packet instructions, on low heat once boiling, until tender.
Keep covered and warm while preparing the stir-fry.

stages.title: Mix sauce
steps: Stir oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar together.
Chop garlic and chilli finely so they release flavour quickly.

stages.title: Stir-fry chicken
steps: Heat oil in a wok over high heat and briefly fry garlic and chilli.
Add chicken mince, breaking it up and cooking until fully cooked through to 75°C.

stages.title: Finish with basil
steps: Add sauce and toss until it coats the meat and reduces slightly.
Turn off heat, fold in basil and serve over rice.

tips: Holy basil gives the most traditional peppery aroma.
variations: Use minced pork or crumbled firm tofu instead.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Arancini
summary: Crisp golden rice balls filled with savoury risotto and melting cheese.
method: Chill the cooked risotto rice until firm. Cube the mozzarella and simmer the passata until thick, so the filling won't leak.
With damp hands, flatten a portion of rice, add a mozzarella cube and a teaspoon of passata, then seal into a ball.
Roll each ball in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Press crumbs over any cracks and chill briefly if soft.
Heat the oil to 170–175°C and fry in batches until golden and piping hot inside.
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with the Parmesan before serving.

stages.title: Prepare filling
steps: Chill risotto thoroughly so it is firm enough to shape.
Cut mozzarella into small cubes and keep the passata thick to prevent leaking.

stages.title: Shape balls
steps: With damp hands flatten a portion of rice in your palm.
Add a cube of mozzarella and a teaspoon of sauce, then seal tightly into a ball.

stages.title: Bread evenly
steps: Roll each ball in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Press crumbs onto any cracks and chill briefly if soft.

stages.title: Fry and drain
steps: Heat oil to 170–175°C and fry in batches until golden and piping hot inside.
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with Parmesan before serving.

tips: Cold, thick risotto makes shaping much easier.
variations: Fill with cooked mushrooms and peas instead of tomato sauce.
storage: Refrigerate cooked arancini up to 2 days; reheat in oven.

title: Aloo gobi
summary: Cauliflower and potatoes cooked with turmeric, cumin, ginger and fragrant Indian spices.
method: Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sizzle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. Add the potatoes and cook until the edges start to colour.
Add the onion, ginger and garlic and cook until softened. Stir in the turmeric and ground coriander briefly.
Add the cauliflower, tomatoes and a splash of water. Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the potatoes and cauliflower are tender, about 15 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for about 5 minutes, until the moisture has cooked off and the spices cling to the vegetables. Season and finish with the coriander leaves.

stages.title: Start potatoes
steps: Heat oil in a wide pan over medium heat and sizzle cumin seeds for 20 seconds.
Add potatoes and cook over medium heat until edges begin to colour.

stages.title: Add aromatics
steps: Stir in onion, ginger and garlic and cook until softened.
Add turmeric and ground coriander, stirring briefly.

stages.title: Cook cauliflower
steps: Add cauliflower, tomatoes and a splash of water.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring gently, until potatoes and cauliflower are tender.

stages.title: Dry and finish
steps: Remove lid and cook off excess moisture for about 5 minutes, until the spices cling to vegetables.
Season and finish with fresh coriander.

tips: Cut potato smaller than cauliflower so both finish together.
variations: Add peas in the final 5 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat in a pan.

title: Menemen
summary: Soft scrambled eggs cooked with tomatoes, green peppers and Turkish spices, served with bread.
method: Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and green peppers for about 6 minutes, until tender.
Add the grated tomatoes, paprika and salt. Simmer uncovered for about 7 minutes, until the liquid evaporates and the sauce thickens.
Lightly beat the eggs and pour them in. Cook over low heat for about 4 minutes, until softly set and still moist.
Take the pan off the heat before the eggs dry out. Scatter over the parsley and serve with the crusty bread for scooping.

stages.title: Soften peppers
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat and cook onion and peppers until tender.
Avoid high heat so the vegetables sweeten rather than scorch.

stages.title: Reduce tomatoes
steps: Add grated tomatoes, paprika and salt.
Simmer uncovered until excess liquid evaporates and sauce thickens.

stages.title: Add eggs
steps: Beat eggs lightly and pour into tomato mixture.
Stir slowly over low heat until softly set and still moist.

stages.title: Serve hot
steps: Remove pan from heat before eggs become dry.
Sprinkle parsley over and serve with bread for scooping.

tips: Eggs continue cooking in the hot pan, so stop while slightly loose.
variations: Add crumbled feta just before serving.
storage: Best fresh; refrigerate leftovers up to 1 day and reheat thoroughly.

title: Croque monsieur
summary: Toasted ham and cheese sandwich with creamy béchamel and a golden Gruyère crust.
method: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until smooth and thick, then season with the nutmeg.
Spread the sourdough with Dijon mustard, then layer on the ham and half the Gruyère. Close into sandwiches and place on a lined baking tray.
Spoon the béchamel over each sandwich and scatter on the remaining Gruyère.
Bake at 220°C until the bread is crisp and the topping bubbles and browns.
Rest for 2 minutes before cutting, then serve hot with a sharp green salad.

stages.title: Make béchamel
steps: Melt butter over medium heat, stir in flour and cook 1 minute without browning.
Whisk in milk gradually and simmer until smooth and thick; season with nutmeg.

stages.title: Build sandwiches
steps: Spread bread with mustard and layer ham and half the cheese.
Close sandwiches and place on a lined baking tray.

stages.title: Top and bake
steps: Spoon béchamel over each sandwich and scatter remaining cheese on top.
Bake at 220°C until bread is crisp and topping bubbles and browns.

stages.title: Rest briefly
steps: Let sandwiches stand for 2 minutes before cutting.
Serve hot with a sharp green salad.

tips: Use a thick béchamel so it stays on top rather than soaking bread.
variations: Top each with a fried egg for croque madame.
storage: Best fresh; refrigerate assembled unbaked sandwiches up to 1 day.

title: Blueberry muffins
summary: Soft blueberry muffins with tender crumb, juicy berries and lightly golden tops.
method: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a 12-hole muffin tray. Toss the blueberries with the extra tablespoon of flour.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in one bowl. In another, whisk the eggs, milk, cooled melted butter and vanilla.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry until no dry flour remains, then gently fold in the blueberries. A few lumps are fine.
Divide the batter among the cases and bake until risen and a skewer comes out without wet batter.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

stages.title: Prepare tins
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C and line a 12-hole muffin tray.
Toss blueberries with a tablespoon of flour to reduce sinking.

stages.title: Mix dry and wet
steps: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in one bowl.
In another, whisk eggs, milk, melted cooled butter and vanilla.

stages.title: Combine batter
steps: Fold wet mixture into dry just until no dry flour remains.
Gently fold in blueberries; a few lumps are desirable.

stages.title: Bake and cool
steps: Divide batter among cases and bake until risen and a skewer comes out without wet batter.
Cool in tin 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack.

tips: Overmixing develops gluten and makes muffins tough.
variations: Replace blueberries with raspberries or chopped apple.
storage: Airtight at room temperature 2 days or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Affogato
summary: Hot espresso poured over cold vanilla ice cream for a simple bittersweet Italian dessert.
method: Chill two serving glasses in the freezer for about 2 minutes, then scoop the vanilla gelato into them.
Brew two fresh espresso shots just before serving, so the coffee is piping hot.
Pour one hot espresso shot over the gelato in each glass.
Top with the grated dark chocolate and crushed amaretti biscuits, then serve straight away with spoons before the gelato melts completely.

stages.title: Chill glasses
steps: Place serving glasses in the freezer briefly so gelato melts more slowly.
Scoop gelato into the chilled glasses.

stages.title: Brew coffee
steps: Prepare two fresh espresso shots immediately before serving.
Keep coffee hot for the contrast against the frozen gelato.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Pour one hot espresso shot over each serving of gelato.
Sprinkle with grated chocolate and crushed amaretti.

stages.title: Serve immediately
steps: Bring glasses to the table straight away.
Serve with spoons so the melting gelato and coffee can be eaten together.

variations: Use decaffeinated espresso or hazelnut gelato.
storage: Assemble only when ready to serve; do not store combined.

title: Sticky toffee pudding
summary: Soft date sponge drenched in warm, buttery toffee sauce.
method: Pour the boiling water over the dates and stir in the bicarbonate of soda. Leave until soft, then mash to a coarse paste.
Beat the butter and brown sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, vanilla and date mixture just until combined.
Pour into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the cream, the sauce brown sugar and the sauce butter in a pan over low heat until dissolved. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until glossy.
Pour the toffee sauce over the warm pudding.

stages.title: Soften dates
steps: Pour boiling water over chopped dates and stir in bicarbonate of soda.
Leave until soft, then mash lightly into a coarse paste.

stages.title: Make batter
steps: Cream butter and brown sugar until fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, vanilla and date mixture just until combined.

stages.title: Bake sponge
steps: Pour into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Rest 5 minutes while making sauce.

stages.title: Make toffee sauce
steps: Heat cream, extra brown sugar and butter gently until dissolved.
Simmer 3–4 minutes until glossy, then pour over warm pudding.

tips: Do not overbake; the date sponge should remain moist.
variations: Add a pinch of sea salt to the sauce.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat portions with sauce.

title: French chocolate mousse
summary: Airy dark chocolate mousse with a silky texture and intense cocoa flavour.
method: Melt the chocolate in a heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water on low heat. Take it off the heat and cool until just warm.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks, not stiff, then refrigerate.
Beat the egg whites with the salt until foamy, then add the sugar gradually. Keep beating until glossy medium peaks form.
Stir the egg yolks and vanilla into the cooled chocolate, then fold in the cream and egg whites in batches.
Divide into glasses and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until set.

stages.title: Melt chocolate
steps: Melt chocolate gently over a pan of barely simmering water.
Remove from heat and cool until just warm, not hot.

stages.title: Whip cream
steps: Whip cold cream to soft peaks and refrigerate briefly.
Avoid stiff peaks, which make folding difficult.

stages.title: Whip egg whites
steps: Beat pasteurised egg whites with salt until foamy, then add sugar gradually.
Continue until glossy medium peaks form.

stages.title: Fold and chill
steps: Stir egg yolks and vanilla into cooled chocolate, then fold in cream and egg whites in batches.
Divide into glasses and refrigerate at least 4 hours before serving.

tips: Use pasteurised eggs because this mousse is not cooked.
variations: Add finely grated orange zest to the chocolate.
storage: Keep refrigerated up to 2 days; do not freeze.
